guided_scaffold_note: Scaffolding for rehearsal or installation execution fades within the session: the first case may be worked with the reference, model, or prompts in view, and the second must be attempted before checking anything. ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g12-arts-and-music-u05-l06

Lesson focus: rehearsal or installation execution

Resource type: ACADEMY_CREATED_SCAFFOLD

GUIDED SCAFFOLD B — support-fading pass for rehearsal or installation execution. Earlier-pass substitute: Loop four events slowly, mark the exact transition that breaks, practise only the two events around it, then return to the full phrase. Mark the relationship involving steady timing as the fragile move, then hide this resource. Make two new studies, loops, maps, or responses without the prompt. Reopen only afterward; compare the order of decisions and the evidence. Report whether the fragile move held. If it did not, use the criteria to name the mismatch without changing the learner’s intent or copying the example. Use it to study rehearsal or installation execution; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached earlier-pass substitute when prior work is unavailable, hide it as directed, and finish both unassisted studies before checking.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use notation, a cue map, paper blocking, silent gesture, or a private live demonstration to one trusted adult as the target permits. When timing or performance control is the target, prose alone does not claim that evidence; the adult may verify the private attempt without recording it. No microphone, camera, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres an aural element (rehearsal or installation execution). Provide a fully equivalent non-aural route: notated, written, or graphic representation; visual or tactile pulse (a moving marker, a tapped or felt beat); and vibration or sight-reading in place of listening. Do not require the learner to hear a pitch, interval, or timbre to demonstrate understanding of it.

Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries exactly the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording. A written or notated account of the intended performance is a full substitute.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.fallback: Use the complete supplied beat map, script, evidence record, or event description. No teacher handout or outside search is required.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce rehearsal or installation execution to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one steady timing relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact steady timing evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from steady timing, accurate events, phrasing, dynamics, articulation, recovery, and interpretive intent; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply rehearsal or installation execution under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on rehearsal or installation execution rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_instruction.title: What rehearsal or installation execution means here
concept_instruction.body: Performance turns a preserved plan into time-based evidence through controlled choices and recovery.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: A short rehearsal loop isolates one demanding moment; slowing, counting, speaking, fingering silently, or mapping events makes the cause of a break easier to notice.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: A faster or more dramatic interpretation may increase energy but reduce control. A secure tempo can reveal phrasing more clearly. Worked example: Loop four events slowly, mark the exact transition that breaks, practise only the two events around it, then return to the full phrase. Non-example: Repeating a whole passage from the beginning without identifying the unstable transition produces volume, not focused rehearsal.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for rehearsal or installation execution is present, but the record does not yet locate steady timing, accurate events, phrasing, dynamics, articulation, recovery, and interpretive intent that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
